environment.description: Same CI/CD pipeline OAuth plugin deployed on ECS Fargate. Origin is placed behind a CloudFront distribution (d1234abcdef.cloudfront.net) with the following configuration: (1) Origin Access Control (OAC) policy type 'Always sign requests' applied to the ALB origin, with the ALB security group restricted to CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing) on port 443 only; (2) CloudFront distribution has a custom cache behavior for /pipeline/auth/* with a CloudFront Function attached at viewer-request stage that validates a signed URL token (using RSA-SHA1 with key pair K3J8X2MPLKEY) — requests without a valid Signature, Key-Pair-Id, and Expires query parameter matching the distribution's trusted key group 'ci-pipeline-signers' are rejected with 403 before reaching origin; (3) The signed URL policy condition restricts the resource pattern to exactly 'https://d1234abcdef.cloudfront.net/pipeline/auth/start?redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fci.internal.corp%2F*' meaning the redirect_uri parameter in the signed URL is locked to paths under ci.internal.corp/ only. Any attempt to craft a redirect_uri pointing to an attacker domain (e.g., attacker.ci.internal.corp or evil.com) would require generating a new signed URL with a different resource pattern, which requires possession of the private key from the trusted key group.

config.origin_access: OAC with 'Always sign requests', ALB SG locked to CloudFront prefix list
config.network: ALB security group allows inbound 443 only from com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing prefix list
